Question 10(c) [12 marks]: What does evidence reveal about religion in Minoan Crete in this period?

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 12):
10–12 marks: Demonstrates a well-developed understanding of what evidence reveals about religion in this period | Demonstrates detailed knowledge and understanding relevant to the question | Integrates evidence from a range of relevant sources to support the response | Communicates ideas and information logically and coherently using a range of appropriate historical terms and concepts
7–9 marks: Demonstrates a clear understanding of what evidence reveals about religion in this period | Demonstrates knowledge and understanding relevant to the question | Uses evidence from a range of relevant sources to support the response | Communicates ideas and information logically using appropriate historical terms and concepts
4–6 marks: Demonstrates some understanding of what evidence reveals about religion in this period | Demonstrates some knowledge relevant to the question | Refers to one or more sources in the response | Communicates ideas using some historical terms and/or concepts
1–3 marks: Makes general statement(s) in relation to the question | May refer to source(s) | May use historical terms and/or concepts


ANSWERS COULD INCLUDE (the student does not need every point):
• Religion appears to have been dominated by the worship of a goddess, depicted in sculpture with snakes.
• Seals and frescoes depict women acting as priestesses, for example the sacred tree and grove fresco.
• Fertility was an important part of Minoan religion, shown through votive objects found near peak sanctuaries.
• Processions may have formed part of religious ceremonies, as shown through frescoes.
• Dancing and bull-leaping are depicted on a variety of sources including sculpture, frescoes, seals, showing the possible inclusion in religious worship.
• The natural world was important to Minoan religion. Depictions of trees, animals, birds on seals and frescoes are frequent. Peak sanctuaries and caves were used for worship.
